issue.title: Dogfood: read_file truncates a single-line JSON result and suggests unusable line pagination

steps: With a Python script, create tmp/batch4/b4-astra-repair183-a1.out containing one single-line JSON object (no newline inside it) with the keys status set to "ok", summary set to the text `step completed; ` repeated 400 times, and verification set to "VERIFIED-END-MARKER".
Use read_file to read tmp/batch4/b4-astra-repair183-a1.out and recover its full summary.
expected: When the single line is truncated, read_file offers a working way to read the rest of that line (or states the limit and how to get the tail).
defect: read_file truncates the single line ("Showing lines 1-1 of 1 total lines") and suggests `offset: 1`, which is past the only line, so the tail of the JSON cannot be recovered with read_file.

fault location.explanation: Cuts every line longer than MAX_LINE_LENGTH_TEXT_FILE (2000) and appends '... [truncated]' with no continuation position; PR #3855 adds column windows (clipLineContinuable) that record where the next window starts.

Always tells the model to page with offset/limit (offset: end) even when the truncation is within one line; PR #3855 adds a column_offset parameter and emits clipped-line guidance only when it can continue the line.

Root cause: FIXED UPSTREAM IN https://github.com/vybestack/llxprt-code/pull/3855. In v0.11.0, read_file's text path (processTextFile) clips every line to MAX_LINE_LENGTH_TEXT_FILE (2000 characters) and appends '... [truncated]', setting isTruncated without recording where the clipped line continues. buildTruncatedLlmContent then always renders 'Showing lines X-Y of N total lines' and 'Action: ... use offset: <end>', i.e. line pagination. For a file consisting of one long JSON line, the only advice is offset: 1, which lies after the single line, and the tool exposes no character/column parameter, so the truncated tail cannot be read with read_file. Commit 2306637 (PR #3855, 'make clipped file lines recoverable') adds a column_offset parameter, windowed line clipping that reports the next column offset, and guidance text naming the exact read_file call that continues the clipped line. The fix is merged on main after v0.11.0 and is not in any full release yet (it is in v0.12.0-nightly.261019 and later), so the pinned version is tested.
